lastText: File ClosedThe Raids Not FlownContestedAllied Combined Chiefs, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) — filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945 — slower than the historical May 1945, the price of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, riskier road instead. The campaign's human cost lands close to the historical one on the Western front — lighter, by a wide margin, than the war the Soviet Union fought over the same years. The February 1945 eastern-city raids were declined — Dresden never becomes the word it became, and the oil and rail campaigns finished the war's arithmetic without it, exactly as their own advocates' logic implied they could. Shingle was cancelled and the landing craft kept for Overlord — no wildcat, no stranded whale, and a Gustav Line ground down frontally instead. The Transportation Plan was restricted to targets clear of population centers — fewer of the civilians the invasion came to liberate killed in its preparation, at a price paid on the beaches in German divisions arriving days earlier. What was really being decided, choice by choice, was never whether Germany lost — only what the peace on the other side of it would look like.One Year LaterA year past victory in Europe, the machinery of occupation is running on the arrangements this campaign's own conferences — Tehran, Yalta, the ones this command actually attended — settled or failed to settle in advance
